title: fix(cli): with the stdio MCP transport on, a host plugin's console output while serving a call reaches stderr
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoMCxdawQGnnkJzSxjJDRc6f)_

Fixes #32942

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：stdio MCP 模式下，宿主插件在处理工具调用时写的 `console.log` / `console.info` / `console.debug` / `process.stdout.write` 现在都会出现在 stderr；stdout 仍然只有 JSON-RPC 帧。
- 为什么改：MCP 客户端一启动就发 `initialize`，收到答复立刻发 `tools/call`，这些调用在 `serve` 的“启动静默窗口”还没关闭时就被处理了，窗口把它们的日志当成启动噪音直接丢掉，两个流都看不到（拦截器审计日志因此在 stdio 部署上全部丢失）。
- 风险与回滚：小。只在 stdio 传输接管 stdout 之后才放行；HTTP 启动完全不变（有对照用例）。代价：stdio 启动时，传输接管之后、横幅之前的启动杂讯（本夹具上 23 行 `[Registry]`）也会直接打到 stderr。回滚 = revert 本 PR，不涉及数据。
- 先看：`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` 的 `quietHolds` 与 `isProtocolStdoutClaimed`；`packages/mcp/src/protocol-stdout.ts` 的 `PROTOCOL_STDOUT_CLAIM` 标记；`packages/cli/test/serve-stdio-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts` 新增的 `#32942` 一组。
- 两分钟验证：`OS_TEST_TIERS=nightly pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run test/serve-stdio-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts`（先 build cli），预期 3/3 通过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

**The mechanism, measured at `origin/main` (`b22be279`).** It is not the stdout redirect and not the transport's stdout claim. It is `serve`'s boot-quiet window. A stdio client writes `initialize` at spawn and its first `tools/call` as soon as that is answered. The transport attaches inside `runtime.start()`, and the window closes about 100 ms after `runtime.start()` returns. So the first calls are served while the window is still open. During the window `console.log` and `console.debug` are replaced by no-ops, and `process.stdout.write` is filtered down to kernel-logger records for the post-banner replay. A host interceptor's line is not one of those records, so it was dropped and reached neither stream. `console.warn` and `console.error` go to stderr directly and were never affected, which is why the card saw the MCP WARN but not the interceptor line.

- **`@objectstack/mcp`**, `protocol-stdout.ts`: `protocolStdout()` now sets a mark on `process.stdout` (`PROTOCOL_STDOUT_CLAIM`, a `Symbol.for` key) when the stdio transport claims the stream. The mark is set before `connect()` attaches stdin, so no call can be served before it exists. `mcp-server-runtime.ts` is not edited.
- **`@objectstack/cli`**, `serve.ts`: the window's stdout and console wrappers ask `quietHolds()` (the window is open AND stdout is not claimed) per write, instead of `bootQuiet`. From the claim on, bytes go to `origStdoutWrite`, which is the stderr forwarder `redirectStdoutToStderr()` installed, never to the real stdout. `isProtocolStdoutClaimed()` reads the mark by key so `serve` does not import the MCP package to ask.
- **Unchanged:** the redirect itself; the window before the claim (every plugin's `init()` and the starts ahead of the MCP plugin are still held back under stdio); the whole window on a boot without the stdio transport; `printDiagnostic` (serve's own lines) stays suppressed while `bootQuiet` is set.

**Each channel after the fix, under stdio, from a call served inside the window** (all measured by the pin): `console.log`, `console.info`, `console.debug` and `process.stdout.write` reach stderr through the forwarder; `console.warn` and `console.error` reach stderr as before. None reaches stdout. From a timer after the banner every channel already reached stderr at `main`, and still does.

## Tests

- `packages/mcp/src/protocol-stdout.test.ts` (+1): `protocolStdout()` sets the mark on `process.stdout` under `Symbol.for('@objectstack/mcp:protocol-stdout-claimed')`, and the mark is absent before the call.
- `packages/cli/test/serve-stdio-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts`, the existing child-process harness for this seam (built `bin/run.js`, a real minted `osk_` key), new top-level `describe` with two cases. The shared `beforeAll` / `afterAll` moved from inside the #7915 `describe` to file level, unchanged, so both describes use one minting boot. The fixture config gains a host plugin whose tool-call interceptor writes through all six channels. With `FX_HOLD_FOR_CALL=1` it holds `kernel:ready` until a call is served (cap 30 s), so the call lands inside the window deterministically instead of racing it. The #7915 case makes no tool call, so the plugin is inert there.
  - **stdio:** `initialize` at spawn, `tools/call list_objects` the moment its answer is read. Every channel's `[fx-call] CHANNEL stdio:list_objects` line is on stderr AND before `Server is ready`. Every stdout line parses as a JSON-RPC frame. `[fx-boot-chatter]` from `init()` is on neither stream.
  - **CONTROL, HTTP:** the same plugin over `POST /api/v1/mcp` after boot: every channel's line on stderr, stdout empty, `[fx-boot-chatter]` still held back.
  - Both run at `OS_LOG_LEVEL=warn`. The #7915 case runs at `info`, a verbose level at which `serve` never opens the window, so the defect cannot be reached there.

## Acceptance notes

- Ruling grep (`ruling|Ruling-ref|maintainer|⛔`) on the touched surface: `serve.ts` has 65 hits, none in the redirect or window region (L2160 to L2850 before the edit, the closest are L2158 "never a second copy", L2328, L2342, L2387 on the port flags). `protocol-stdout.ts` and its test have 0. The e2e file has 3, all in the existing #7915 harness text. `mcp-server-runtime.ts` (13 hits) is not edited.
- Cost under stdio, stated because it is real: whatever the boot writes to the console after the transport claims stdout is no longer held back. On this fixture that is 23 `[Registry]` `console.log` lines and one `WARN` that now print on stderr before the banner instead of being dropped (the `WARN` was replayed under the banner before). The stream cannot tell a call's line from the rest of the boot. Holding them would mean marking request context in the MCP runtime's dispatch, outside this card's surface. Nothing reaches stdout either way.
- The pin lives in a `.e2e` file, so it runs on the nightly tier, the same tier as the #7915 purity pin it sits beside. The file is now about 19 s of local wall (four boots) and declares no `test-budget` line, as before this PR. Flagged for the seat: whether it needs one now.
- HTTP requests served before the window closes would lose their console lines the same way, but an HTTP client does not normally reach a server before its banner, and the card's HTTP control prints the line. Left as is; no change on the HTTP path.
- The card reproduced through `os start`; `start` spawns `serve` with inherited stdio, so the fix is in `serve`. Both doors were measured before and after.

## Verification

Readings at head `f4bbd648` (fix commits on `b22be279`; `origin/main` merged once before opening, no overlap with this diff).

<details><summary>Measured at origin/main first (the premise holds, with a sharper mechanism)</summary>

A scratch app with the card's interceptor plugin plus a timer that writes through every channel 4 to 8 s after boot, a minted key, `OS_MCP_STDIO_ENABLED=true`:

- Calls written after the banner (my first harness): the `[qa-interceptor]` line and every timer line on stderr, under both `os serve --dev` and `os start --no-ui`. Not reproduced.
- Calls written the way an SDK client writes them (`initialize` at spawn, `tools/call` on its answer, before the banner): `os serve` and `os start` both answered `list_objects` and denied `delete_record` (PERMISSION_DENIED from the interceptor), stdout carried 3 frames and nothing else, and the interceptor's `console.log` line was on NEITHER stream. A `process.stderr.write` line from the same interceptor was on stderr. Reproduced on both doors.
- Never observed: a non-frame line on stdout. The defect loses lines; it does not corrupt the protocol stream.

After the fix, same harness: the `[qa-interceptor]` lines on stderr on both doors, stdout 3 frames only.

</details>

<details><summary>Package tests, typecheck, lint, derived gates</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp test`: Test Files 64 passed (64), Tests 1138 passed (1138)
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2`: Test Files 416 passed (416), Tests 5934 passed (5934)
- `OS_TEST_TIERS=nightly … vitest run test/serve-stdio-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts`: Tests 3 passed (3)
- `pnpm lint`: exit 0
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 72 families derived; 70 exit 0, 2 NOT MEASURED (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needs `dist/` for packages outside this closure, `check:i18n-coverage` a partial lint round). `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` first exited 3 on the shallow clone, and passed (48 cases) after fetching its pinned fixture commit. `--ran` reconciliation: 72 derived, 70 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
- The `integration` tier of `packages/cli` is declared to CI.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (both red, both restored)</summary>

The e2e spawns the built CLI, which loads both packages from `dist/`, so each leg was rebuilt and checked with `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`.

- **serve ignores the claim:** `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on `serve.ts`, anchor `const quietHolds = () => bootQuiet && !isProtocolStdoutClaimed();` (x1 to x0) replaced by `const quietHolds = () => bootQuiet;`. Rebuilt; preflight: marker absent from all 952 built files. Result: **1 failed, 2 passed**: the stdio case, `the console.log line of the stdio call is missing from stderr`; the #7915 case and the HTTP CONTROL stayed green. Restored: blob == HEAD (`5d4e3372`), `git diff HEAD` empty, rebuilt, preflight marker present.
- **the mark removed:** the one line that sets `PROTOCOL_STDOUT_CLAIM` to `true` on the stream deleted (x1 to x0). mcp unit: **1 failed, 2 passed** (the new mark case). mcp rebuilt, preflight absent from all 12 built files; e2e: **1 failed, 2 passed**, the stdio case with the same message, which pins the key both packages spell. Restored: blob == HEAD (`5cc99b80`), `git diff HEAD` empty, rebuilt, preflight marker present in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`.

</details>
